correctness.rationale: Fourier alias blocks diagonalize the full Gram solve exactly. For every nonzero frequency residue the neglected alias kernel mass is \(O((r/N)^{2\alpha})\), the nonsmooth density has Fourier coefficients \(O((1+|h|)^{-2})\), and summing the distortion over residues is \(O(N^{-1})\). The resulting weight error is \(O(N^{-2})\); only \(O(1)\) sample nodes can have negative weights because the nonnegative periodization density vanishes linearly at two points. The zero-alias block yields exactly \(2\gamma\zeta(2\alpha)\) as the scaled total-mass deficit; fixed even N and gamma tending to infinity gives a negative endpoint weight. The independent Gram-solve and Fourier diagnostics passed 283 checks. Finite checks are supplementary and not the infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The full 2026 construction and its explicit multivariate positivity gap were compared at the level of exact weights and definitions. The relevant 2010 periodic Sobolev interpolation paper was inspected through its full public text; its Section 8 gives equal-weight quadrature for integration against Lebesgue measure, not signed-weight asymptotics for the sine-squared periodization density. Published related weighted and universal lattice quadrature rules use other spaces or estimators, not this high-order full-lattice signed weight law. Existing earlier one-dimensional first-order finite-grid classification only treats \(\alpha=1\) and cannot imply the \(\alpha\ge2\) theorem. Published mathematical-record searches did not return a directly covering high-order finding. Priority risks remain for unindexed equivalences; absence of search hits is not a proof of novelty.

value.rationale: The motivating 2026 work identifies asymptotic positivity as a stability gap. The analysis supplies a quantified negative-mass bound and asymptotic norm control for the higher-order univariate construction, an exact normalizing-constant law, and a finite-grid parameter-boundary counterexample. These results address signed coefficient stability rather than re-running a quadrature accuracy estimate. They do not claim to solve the multivariate algorithm or assert eventual pointwise positivity.
